q: In the DOH technical manual, which Room Data Sheet gives the ideal environmental conditions (air, sound, lighting, safety)?
o: Room Data Sheet D: Equipment Schedule
Room Data Sheet C: Layout of Room and Space Components
Room Data Sheet B: Technical Design Data
Room Data Sheet A: Functional Design Requirements
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, items 1.2 and 2.2
n: A = functional; B = environmental technical data; C = services, floor/wall demands and layout. Remember this: every room has three sheets: A = Activities (functional), B = Bodily comfort (air, sound, light, safety), C = Construction (services, floor/wall demands, layout). "Temperate" is 15–27°C, the Philippine comfort band.

q: Which Room Data Sheet lists activities involved, people involved and planning relationships?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.1

q: Under the manual's outdoor temperature ranges, what is "temperate"?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.1.1a
n: Cold <10, cool 10–15, temperate 15–27, hot 27–38, very hot >38.

q: What relative humidity range does the manual call "humid"?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.1.6a
n: Very dry 0–25, dry 25–50, humid 50–75, very humid 75–100.

q: One Ton of Refrigeration (TR), as used for cooling load in the manual, equals:
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.1.7
n: Cooling load in TR, 1 TR = 12,660 kJ/hr.

q: What acceptable noise level range applies to intensive care and recovery areas?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.2.1a (Table 1)

q: What noise range is acceptable for light maintenance shops, kitchens and laundry areas?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.2.1a (Table 1)

q: In the common noise levels table, what sound level is the threshold of pain?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.2.1b (Table II)
n: 120 dB threshold of pain; 110 dB threshold of discomfort; 0 dB threshold of audibility.

q: When task lighting is used with general lighting, the general lighting should be at least what percentage of the task level?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.3.3
n: At least 20% of the local level, so task light becomes supplementary.

q: Who fills out the "Space Demands" and "Regulations and Notes" portions of Room Data Sheet C?
o: The designer, based on end-users' needs and local laws
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, items 2.3.4–2.3.5
n: They are left for the designer because needs vary per project.

q: Up to what capacity may the Level 2 manual's guidelines on clinical ancillary and support services be used?
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 1.6
n: The manual is for a 100-bed Level 2, but ancillary/support guidelines can be used up to 250 beds.

q: A designer checks an RDS B sheet that lists "Pressure Differential: Negative 10 Pa." What kind of room is this most likely?
o: An isolation room for infectious patients
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.2.1.4; DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 250-Bed Hospital (Level 3), 1st ed. 2017, Vol. 3, 250B-ER-RDS-06B
n: Negative pressure is required in infectious rooms so contaminated air is exhausted out.

q: Match the sheet: "direct demands on floor and wall" →
ref: DOH Manual on Technical Guidelines, 100-Bed Hospital (Level 2), 2nd ed. 2014, Vol. 1, item 2.3
n: C = construction side. Remember this: every room has three sheets: A = Activities (functional), B = Bodily comfort (air, sound, light, safety), C = Construction (services, floor/wall demands, layout). "Temperate" is 15–27°C, the Philippine comfort band.
